quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Sarah your phone is ringing
quests.punctuatedSentence: Sarah, your phone is ringing.
quests.ruleExplanation: When you address someone by name at the start of a sentence, a comma sets their name apart from the rest of the message.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence is speaking directly to someone by name before the message begins.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Sarah your phone is ringing ➔ Final: Sarah, your phone is ringing.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Dad dinner is ready
quests.punctuatedSentence: Dad, dinner is ready.
quests.ruleExplanation: A name used to call someone's attention, like 'Dad,' is followed by a comma even in a short sentence.
quests.nativeTip: Notice that the sentence isn't about 'Dad' - it's spoken to him.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Dad dinner is ready ➔ Final: Dad, dinner is ready.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Coach were ready for the drill
quests.punctuatedSentence: Coach, we're ready for the drill.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even a title like 'coach' used to address someone directly is separated with a comma, and 'we're' needs its apostrophe for 'we are.'
quests.nativeTip: A title used to speak directly to someone works the same way as using their name.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Coach were ready for the drill ➔ Final: Coach, we're ready for the drill.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Can you pass the salt Grandpa
quests.punctuatedSentence: Can you pass the salt, Grandpa?
quests.ruleExplanation: When the name of the person being addressed comes at the end of a sentence, a comma still separates it from the rest of the sentence.
quests.nativeTip: This time, the name being called comes after the request, not before it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Can you pass the salt Grandpa ➔ Final: Can you pass the salt, Grandpa?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I really appreciate your help Maria
quests.punctuatedSentence: I really appreciate your help, Maria.
quests.ruleExplanation: A name placed at the end of a sentence to address someone is set off with a comma before it.
quests.nativeTip: Look for who is being spoken to, even though their name appears last.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I really appreciate your help Maria ➔ Final: I really appreciate your help, Maria.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: That was a great game Coach
quests.punctuatedSentence: That was a great game, Coach.
quests.ruleExplanation: Just like a name, a title used to address someone at the end of a sentence needs a comma before it.
quests.nativeTip: The title at the end still marks who the sentence is being said to.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: That was a great game Coach ➔ Final: That was a great game, Coach.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I think Jake you should try out for the team
quests.punctuatedSentence: I think, Jake, you should try out for the team.
quests.ruleExplanation: A name that interrupts a sentence in the middle is set off with a comma both before and after it.
quests.nativeTip: This time the name interrupts the sentence in the middle - it needs to be boxed in on both sides.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I think Jake you should try out for the team ➔ Final: I think, Jake, you should try out for the team.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: You know Grandma this soup is my favorite
quests.punctuatedSentence: You know, Grandma, this soup is my favorite.
quests.ruleExplanation: When someone's name appears mid-sentence, commas surround it to show that the address interrupts the main thought.
quests.nativeTip: Find where the name breaks into the sentence, then mark both sides of it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: You know Grandma this soup is my favorite ➔ Final: You know, Grandma, this soup is my favorite.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Please remember Lucas to lock the door
quests.punctuatedSentence: Please remember, Lucas, to lock the door.
quests.ruleExplanation: A mid-sentence direct address is enclosed by commas on both sides, even inside a short instruction.
quests.nativeTip: The listener's name breaks up the sentence right in the middle of the instruction.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Please remember Lucas to lock the door ➔ Final: Please remember, Lucas, to lock the door.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Well I suppose we could try again tomorrow
quests.punctuatedSentence: Well, I suppose we could try again tomorrow.
quests.ruleExplanation: A mild interjection like 'well' is followed by a comma when the rest of the sentence stays calm.
quests.nativeTip: This opening word expresses a mild reaction before a calm statement continues.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Well I suppose we could try again tomorrow ➔ Final: Well, I suppose we could try again tomorrow.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Ouch that really hurt
quests.punctuatedSentence: Ouch! That really hurt.
quests.ruleExplanation: A strong interjection like 'ouch' can stand alone with an exclamation mark, separate from the sentence that follows.
quests.nativeTip: This reaction is sudden and intense enough to stand completely on its own.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Ouch that really hurt ➔ Final: Ouch! That really hurt.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Oh I didnt realize you were still here
quests.punctuatedSentence: Oh, I didn't realize you were still here.
quests.ruleExplanation: A mild interjection like 'oh' is followed by a comma rather than an exclamation mark, and 'didn't' needs its apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This soft reaction eases into the sentence rather than exploding on its own.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Oh I didnt realize you were still here ➔ Final: Oh, I didn't realize you were still here.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Yikes that traffic looks terrible
quests.punctuatedSentence: Yikes! That traffic looks terrible.
quests.ruleExplanation: A sudden, strong reaction like 'yikes' stands alone with an exclamation mark rather than blending into the sentence with a comma.
quests.nativeTip: This word reacts strongly and suddenly, more than a soft comment would.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Yikes that traffic looks terrible ➔ Final: Yikes! That traffic looks terrible.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Hmm Im not sure thats the right answer
quests.punctuatedSentence: Hmm, I'm not sure that's the right answer.
quests.ruleExplanation: A thoughtful, mild interjection like 'hmm' takes a comma, since the tone stays calm rather than urgent.
quests.nativeTip: This reaction shows quiet thought, not sudden shock.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Hmm Im not sure thats the right answer ➔ Final: Hmm, I'm not sure that's the right answer.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Ah I finally understand the instructions
quests.punctuatedSentence: Ah, I finally understand the instructions.
quests.ruleExplanation: A soft interjection expressing realization, like 'ah,' is followed by a comma rather than an exclamation mark.
quests.nativeTip: Compare the tone here to a sudden shock - is this reaction closer to alarm or quiet realization?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Ah I finally understand the instructions ➔ Final: Ah, I finally understand the instructions.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Hey Jamie did you get my message
quests.punctuatedSentence: Hey, Jamie, did you get my message?
quests.ruleExplanation: Both the interjection 'hey' and the name 'Jamie' are set off with commas, and the sentence ends with a question mark since it's asking something.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence opens with a casual interjection and immediately names who it's talking to.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Hey Jamie did you get my message ➔ Final: Hey, Jamie, did you get my message?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Well Dad I think we should leave now
quests.punctuatedSentence: Well, Dad, I think we should leave now.
quests.ruleExplanation: The interjection 'well' and the direct address 'Dad' are each followed by their own comma.
quests.nativeTip: Two separate elements open this sentence before the main statement begins.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Well Dad I think we should leave now ➔ Final: Well, Dad, I think we should leave now.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Oh Grandma that story always makes me laugh
quests.punctuatedSentence: Oh, Grandma, that story always makes me laugh.
quests.ruleExplanation: A gentle interjection combined with a direct address needs a comma after each part.
quests.nativeTip: Identify both the reaction word and the name being addressed at the start.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Oh Grandma that story always makes me laugh ➔ Final: Oh, Grandma, that story always makes me laugh.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: This plan I think will actually work
quests.punctuatedSentence: This plan, I think, will actually work.
quests.ruleExplanation: A conversational aside like 'I think' inserted into the middle of a sentence is separated by commas on both sides.
quests.nativeTip: A short opinion breaks into the middle of the sentence - box it in with commas.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: This plan I think will actually work ➔ Final: This plan, I think, will actually work.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The new schedule you know starts on Monday
quests.punctuatedSentence: The new schedule, you know, starts on Monday.
quests.ruleExplanation: Casual interrupting phrases such as 'you know' are set off with commas because they can be removed without changing the sentence's core meaning.
quests.nativeTip: This casual phrase interrupts the sentence without changing its main meaning.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The new schedule you know starts on Monday ➔ Final: The new schedule, you know, starts on Monday.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The weather if you ask me looks like rain
quests.punctuatedSentence: The weather, if you ask me, looks like rain.
quests.ruleExplanation: An inserted opinion phrase like 'if you ask me' is enclosed in commas because it interrupts the main sentence.
quests.nativeTip: This phrase adds the speaker's opinion but could be removed from the sentence entirely.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The weather if you ask me looks like rain ➔ Final: The weather, if you ask me, looks like rain.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Please be careful Dad
quests.punctuatedSentence: Please be careful, Dad!
quests.ruleExplanation: The direct address 'Dad' takes a comma, and the urgency of the plea calls for an exclamation mark instead of a period.
quests.nativeTip: The plea here carries worry, not a calm request.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Please be careful Dad ➔ Final: Please be careful, Dad!

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Are you all right Grandma
quests.punctuatedSentence: Are you all right, Grandma?
quests.ruleExplanation: The name 'Grandma' is set off with a comma, and the sentence ends with a question mark because it's asking something.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence checks on someone directly by name, and it's clearly a question.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Are you all right Grandma ➔ Final: Are you all right, Grandma?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I missed you so much Sam
quests.punctuatedSentence: I missed you so much, Sam!
quests.ruleExplanation: The name 'Sam' takes a comma, and the strong emotion in the sentence calls for an exclamation mark rather than a period.
quests.nativeTip: The strength of feeling here goes beyond a plain statement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I missed you so much Sam ➔ Final: I missed you so much, Sam!

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Conversational Interruptions & List Commas (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The trip plans I believe include Paris Rome and Venice
quests.punctuatedSentence: The trip plans, I believe, include Paris, Rome, and Venice.
quests.ruleExplanation: The interrupting phrase 'I believe' is set off with commas, and the three listed cities are separated by commas as well.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence has both an inserted opinion and a list of cities - handle each comma job.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The trip plans I believe include Paris Rome and Venice ➔ Final: The trip plans, I believe, include Paris, Rome, and Venice.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Well Lisa I dont think we should wait any longer
quests.punctuatedSentence: Well, Lisa, I don't think we should wait any longer.
quests.ruleExplanation: The interjection 'well' and the direct address 'Lisa' each take a comma, and 'don't' needs its apostrophe.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs commas for the opening interjection and name, plus a fix to a shortened word.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Well Lisa I dont think we should wait any longer ➔ Final: Well, Lisa, I don't think we should wait any longer.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: This recipe Mia isnt as hard as it looks
quests.punctuatedSentence: This recipe, Mia, isn't as hard as it looks.
quests.ruleExplanation: The mid-sentence direct address 'Mia' is boxed in by commas, and 'isn't' needs an apostrophe for 'is not.'
quests.nativeTip: The listener's name interrupts the sentence in the middle, and a contraction nearby is missing its apostrophe.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: This recipe Mia isnt as hard as it looks ➔ Final: This recipe, Mia, isn't as hard as it looks.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Hey Mom can you believe how big hes gotten
quests.punctuatedSentence: Hey, Mom, can you believe how big he's gotten?
quests.ruleExplanation: The interjection 'hey' and the direct address 'Mom' each take a comma, 'he's' needs its apostrophe, and the sentence ends with a question mark since it's asking something.
quests.nativeTip: This message opens with an interjection and a name, then asks something with real feeling behind it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Hey Mom can you believe how big hes gotten ➔ Final: Hey, Mom, can you believe how big he's gotten?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: This decision honestly wasnt easy for the team
quests.punctuatedSentence: This decision, honestly, wasn't easy for the team.
quests.ruleExplanation: The interrupting phrase 'honestly' is set off with commas, and 'wasn't' needs an apostrophe for 'was not.'
quests.nativeTip: An opinion interrupts the middle of this sentence, and a contraction nearby needs fixing.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: This decision honestly wasnt easy for the team ➔ Final: This decision, honestly, wasn't easy for the team.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Congratulations Uncle Ray on the new job
quests.punctuatedSentence: Congratulations, Uncle Ray, on the new job!
quests.ruleExplanation: The direct address 'Uncle Ray' is set off with commas on both sides, and the celebratory tone calls for an exclamation mark instead of a period.
quests.nativeTip: A title and name are being addressed directly, and the occasion calls for real enthusiasm.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Congratulations Uncle Ray on the new job ➔ Final: Congratulations, Uncle Ray, on the new job!
